Reuters | 25 September 2026, 20:36 UTC
Iran's Araqchi says now up to US to accept 7-day plan

Sept 25 (Reuters) - Iran has given the United States a "concrete" seven-day plan to open the strategic Strait of Hormuz and the choice now rests with the US, Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi told reporters at the United Nations on Friday.

"If the necessary conditions are met, the strait can be reopened, a normal maritime passage restored within seven days. The choice now rests with the United States," he said.

"The actions that the United States should take are not new. They are all already in the MOU," he said, referring to the memorandum of understanding that Iran and the United States agreed in June.
